title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Training Note — Lateness Share of a Re-Rated Revolving Late Fee
content:
**What is the lateness share?** When the most recent late fee on a Ridgeline Pro Credit revolving account is re-rated, the fee is scaled by how far past due the latest closed statement shows the account and by whether a principal's personal guarantee is on file.

**How is it set?**

| Days past due on the latest closed statement | Personal guarantee on file | Lateness share |
|---|---|---|
| No more than 5 | Yes | Prorated: the statement's days past due divided by 10 |
| No more than 5 | No | 0.75, a flat standard share whatever the days late |
| More than 5 | Either | 1 — the fee is charged whole |

**What does the share multiply?** The scheduled late fee after every dollar reduction taken off it, that reduced fee never below zero. The product is rounded to the nearest cent, and that is the re-rated late fee.

**Where are the inputs read?** The days past due from the latest closed statement of the account; the guarantee from the account record.

**Worked cases (hypothetical, scheduled fee after reductions 30.00)**

| Days past due | Guarantee | Share | Re-rated late fee |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | On file | 0.3 | 9.00 |
| 5 | On file | 0.5 | 15.00 |
| 5 | Not on file | 0.75 | 22.50 |
| 6 | On file | 1 | 30.00 |
